notes:
1. Basic Facts
  • India is located in South Asia.
  • It lies entirely in the Northern Hemisphere.
  • It also lies entirely in the Eastern Hemisphere.
  • India occupies a central position at the head of the Indian Ocean.
  • The Indian peninsula projects southward into the Indian Ocean.
  • The Arabian Sea lies to the west of India.
  • The Bay of Bengal lies to the east.
  • The Indian Ocean lies to the south.

India's location between West Asia, Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean gives it major geographical and strategic importance.

2. Area of India
  • India's geographical area is approximately 3.28 million square kilometres.
  • The official figure commonly used is 3,287,263 sq km.
  • India is the seventh-largest country in the world by area.
  • It occupies about 2.4% of the world's total geographical land area.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

India → 3.28 million sq km → 7th largest country

3. Countries Larger than India

The six countries larger than India by area are:

  • Russia.
  • Canada.
  • China.
  • United States.
  • Brazil.
  • Australia.

India comes next as the seventh largest.

📌 Memory

Russia → Canada → China/USA → Brazil → Australia → India

4. Latitudinal Extent

The standard NCERT geographical extent of mainland India is:

  • Southern latitude → 8°4′ N.
  • Northern latitude → 37°6′ N.

NCERT broadly describes India as extending from about 8°N to 37°N.

📌 Must-Memorise

Mainland India Latitude → 8°4′ N to 37°6′ N

5. Longitudinal Extent

India extends approximately from:

  • Western longitude → 68°7′ E.
  • Eastern longitude → 97°25′ E.
📌 Must-Memorise

India Longitude → 68°7′ E to 97°25′ E

6. Latitudinal Spread
  • India's latitudinal extent is approximately 29°.
  • This large north-south extent creates considerable climatic variation.
  • Southern India lies closer to the Equator.
  • Northern India extends well into the subtropical latitudes.
7. Longitudinal Spread
  • India's longitudinal extent is also approximately 29°.
  • This creates nearly two hours of difference in local solar time between eastern and western India.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

East-West Local Time Difference → Nearly 2 Hours

8. North-South Extent
  • India's north-south distance is approximately 3,214 km.
  • It is measured from the northern extent to the southern mainland extent in standard textbook geography.
📌 Must-Memorise

North–South Extent → 3,214 km

9. East-West Extent
  • India's east-west extent is approximately 2,933 km.
📌 Must-Memorise

East–West Extent → 2,933 km

10. Why North-South Distance Is Greater
  • One degree of latitude has a fairly constant ground distance.
  • The ground distance represented by one degree of longitude decreases away from the Equator.
  • Therefore, India's north-south ground distance is greater than its east-west distance even though both span roughly 29°.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Similar angular extent does not mean similar ground distance.

11. Tropic of Cancer
  • Tropic of Cancer lies at approximately 23°30′ N latitude.
  • It passes through the central part of India.
  • It divides India approximately into tropical and subtropical portions.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tropic of Cancer → 23½° N

From west to east, the Tropic of Cancer passes through eight Indian states:

  • Gujarat.
  • Rajasthan.
  • Madhya Pradesh.
  • Chhattisgarh.
  • Jharkhand.

G R M C J W T M

Number of Indian states crossed by Tropic of Cancer → 8

13. Tamil Nadu and Tropic of Cancer
  • Tropic of Cancer does not pass through Tamil Nadu.
  • Tamil Nadu lies entirely south of the Tropic of Cancer.
  • Therefore, Tamil Nadu lies in the tropical latitudinal zone.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Tropic of Cancer → Does NOT cross Tamil Nadu.

14. Indian Standard Meridian
  • India's Standard Meridian is 82°30′ E longitude.
  • Indian Standard Time is calculated from this meridian.
  • It lies near the central longitudinal part of India.
📌 Must-Memorise

IST Meridian → 82°30′ E

15. Mirzapur and Standard Meridian
  • India's Standard Meridian passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.
  • Mirzapur is commonly used as the reference location in Indian geography questions.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

82°30′ E → Near Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh

16. States Crossed by Standard Meridian

The 82°30′ E meridian passes through or across the longitudinal extent of:

  • Uttar Pradesh.
  • Madhya Pradesh.
  • Chhattisgarh.
  • Odisha.
  • Andhra Pradesh.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Standard Meridian → 5 States

17. Indian Standard Time
  • Indian Standard Time is abbreviated IST.
  • IST is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time/UTC.
  • Therefore:

IST = UTC + 5:30.

📌 Must-Memorise

IST → GMT/UTC + 5 hours 30 minutes

18. Why India Uses One Standard Time
  • Local solar time varies from longitude to longitude.
  • India's east-west extent produces almost a two-hour local-time difference.
  • A single standard time avoids administrative, transport and communication confusion.
19. Arunachal Pradesh and Gujarat Time Difference
  • Sunrise occurs much earlier in Arunachal Pradesh than in Gujarat.
  • Both nevertheless officially follow IST.
  • This is a direct consequence of India's wide longitudinal extent.
20. Southernmost Point of Mainland India
  • Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India.
  • It is located in Tamil Nadu.
  • It lies close to 8°4′ N latitude.
📌 Must-Memorise

Southernmost Mainland India → Kanyakumari

21. Southernmost Point of India
  • Indira Point is the southernmost point of the Indian Union.
  • It is located on Great Nicobar Island.
  • Its latitude is approximately 6°45′ N.
📌 Must-Memorise

Southernmost India → Indira Point

Southernmost Mainland → Kanyakumari

22. Indira Point
  • Indira Point is part of Great Nicobar Island.
  • It lies much farther south than mainland India.
  • It is close to Indonesia's Sumatra region.
  • It was formerly called Pygmalion Point.
23. Indira Point and 2004 Tsunami
  • Indira Point was affected by land subsidence during the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami.
  • Parts of the area were submerged.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Indira Point → Great Nicobar → 2004 Tsunami Impact

24. Western Extreme
  • India's western geographical extent reaches Gujarat.
  • Guhar Moti in the Kutch region of Gujarat is commonly cited in competitive-exam geography as India's westernmost inhabited/extreme-point reference.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Western Extreme → Gujarat

25. Eastern Extreme
  • India's eastern geographical extent lies in Arunachal Pradesh.
  • Locations such as Kibithu/Dong are commonly cited in exam mapping near India's eastern extremity.
  • Arunachal Pradesh experiences sunrise much earlier than western India.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Eastern Extreme → Arunachal Pradesh

26. India and the Equator
  • The Equator does not pass through India.
  • Even India's southernmost territory lies north of the Equator.
  • India therefore lies entirely in the Northern Hemisphere.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Equator → Does NOT cross India.

27. India and Prime Meridian
  • The Prime Meridian is 0° longitude.
  • India lies east of the Prime Meridian.
  • India is therefore entirely in the Eastern Hemisphere.
28. India as a Peninsula
  • A peninsula is a landmass surrounded by water on three sides.
  • Peninsular India is surrounded by:
  • Arabian Sea on the west.
  • Bay of Bengal on the east.
  • Indian Ocean on the south.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

India → Large South Asian Peninsula

29. Indian Ocean
  • India has a uniquely prominent position in the northern Indian Ocean.
  • The ocean itself is named after India.
  • India's peninsular position historically supported maritime connections with Africa, West Asia and Southeast Asia.
30. Strategic Location of India

India lies close to major maritime routes connecting:

  • Europe.
  • West Asia.
  • Africa.
  • South Asia.
  • Southeast Asia.
  • East Asia.

Its location gives India strategic importance in Indian Ocean trade and security.

31. Suez Canal and India
  • The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 significantly shortened the sea route between India and Europe.
  • The canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.
  • It reduced the need to sail around the Cape of Good Hope.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Suez Canal → 1869 → Shorter India–Europe Route

42. Island Maritime Neighbours

India's important maritime neighbours include:

  • Sri Lanka.
  • Maldives.
  • Indonesia also lies close to India's Nicobar Islands across maritime boundaries.
43. India and Sri Lanka
  • Sri Lanka lies southeast of the Indian peninsula.
  • India and Sri Lanka are separated principally by the Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar.
  • The narrowest marine region contains a chain of shoals.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

India–Sri Lanka → Palk Strait + Gulf of Mannar

44. Palk Strait
  • Palk Strait lies between Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka.
  • It connects the Bay of Bengal/Palk Bay region with waters toward the Gulf of Mannar.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Link

Tamil Nadu → India's closest mainland region to Sri Lanka.

45. Gulf of Mannar
  • Gulf of Mannar lies between southeastern Tamil Nadu and western Sri Lanka.
  • It is an important marine-biological region.
  • Detailed biodiversity will be covered in the forest and biodiversity chapter.
46. Adam's Bridge / Rama Setu
  • A chain of limestone shoals occurs between Rameswaram region in India and Mannar region of Sri Lanka.
  • It is known as Adam's Bridge or Rama Setu.
🔗 TNPSC Map Fact

Rameswaram → Pamban Island → Near Sri Lanka

47. India and Maldives
  • Maldives lies southwest of India in the Indian Ocean.
  • It lies south of Lakshadweep.
  • The Eight Degree Channel separates the Minicoy region from the Maldives.
48. Land Boundary Length
  • India's land frontier is commonly given in standard official/exam references as about 15,200 km.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Land Boundary → About 15,200 km

49. India's Coastline — Important Updated Fact

This is now a very important current-exam correction.

  • Older textbooks give India's coastline as 7,516.6 km.
  • In 2025, the Government of India formally promulgated a revised coastline measurement of 11,098.81 km.
  • The reassessment was carried out using modern GIS and high-resolution High-Water-Line data by the National Hydrographic Office in coordination with Survey of India.
📌 MUST UPDATE FOR EXAM

Old figure → 7,516.6 km

Revised official figure → 11,098.81 km

50. Why India's Coastline Length Changed
  • India's physical coast did not suddenly become thousands of kilometres longer.
  • The method and resolution of measurement changed.
  • Modern high-resolution mapping captures small bays, creeks, inlets and irregularities more precisely.
  • The revised coastline was promulgated by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways in April 2025.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Coastline revision → Measurement improvement, not territorial expansion.

51. Largest State Coastline — Updated Figure

Under the revised 2025 measurement:

  • Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states.
  • Gujarat's revised coastline is 2,340.62 km.
📌 Must-Memorise

Longest State Coastline → Gujarat

52. Tamil Nadu Coastline — Updated Figure
  • Tamil Nadu's old commonly cited coastline was approximately 906.9 km.
  • The revised official 2025 measurement is 1,068.69 km.
  • Under the revised figures Tamil Nadu has a slightly longer coastline than Andhra Pradesh.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Tamil Nadu Coastline → 1,068.69 km revised

53. Andhra Pradesh Coastline — Updated Figure
  • Andhra Pradesh's revised coastline is 1,053.07 km.
  • The Government noted that Andhra Pradesh became third among states by coastline length under the revised measurement.
📌 Revised Ranking — Top Three States

Gujarat → 1st.

Tamil Nadu → 2nd.

Andhra Pradesh → 3rd.

54. Island Coastline
  • Andaman and Nicobar Islands have a very long and highly irregular coastline.
  • Their revised coastline is 3,083.50 km.
  • This is longer than the coastline of any individual coastal state, though A&N is a Union Territory.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

State with longest coastline → Gujarat.

State/UT entity with very large coastline → Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

From north to south:

The Indian Union Territories with coastlines include:

  • Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
  • Lakshadweep.
  • Puducherry.
  • Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu through its Daman–Diu coastal territory.

The 2025 official coastline reassessment includes A&N, Lakshadweep, Puducherry and Daman & Diu coastline segments.

59. Andaman and Nicobar Islands
  • Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal/Andaman Sea region.
  • They form India's major eastern island group.
  • They extend in a north-south chain.
  • Great Nicobar is the southernmost major island of the group.
60. Lakshadweep
  • Lakshadweep lies in the Arabian Sea.
  • It is located west of Kerala.
  • It consists primarily of coral islands and atolls.
  • Detailed physical geography will be covered later.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Lakshadweep → Arabian Sea

Andaman & Nicobar → Bay of Bengal side

61. Ten Degree Channel
  • Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman group from the Nicobar group.
  • It lies close to 10° N latitude.
📌 Must-Memorise

10° Channel → Andaman vs Nicobar

62. Nine Degree Channel
  • Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy Island from the main Lakshadweep island group.
📌 Must-Memorise

9° Channel → Minicoy from Rest of Lakshadweep

63. Eight Degree Channel
  • Eight Degree Channel lies between Minicoy and the Maldives region.

64. Duncan Passage
  • Duncan Passage separates South Andaman Island from Little Andaman Island.
🔗 TNPSC Map Fact

Duncan Passage → South Andaman / Little Andaman

65. Indian Ocean Position and Trade

India's central Indian Ocean location historically connected:

  • Persian Gulf and Arabian Peninsula.
  • East African coast.
  • Southeast Asia.
  • Europe through western maritime routes.
  • East Asia through eastern maritime routes.

This geographical position helped the development of long-distance trade and cultural exchanges.

66. India as Part of the Indian Subcontinent

The Indian subcontinent broadly includes India and neighbouring South Asian countries.

Its relative geographical separation is created by:

  • Himalayan mountain systems to the north.
  • Seas and ocean around the peninsula.

The National Portal describes India's mainland physical setting in terms of the great mountain zone, Indo-Gangetic plains, desert and southern peninsula.

67. India's Position Relative to Asia
  • India lies south of the major Himalayan mountain system.
  • It projects into the northern Indian Ocean.
  • This creates a distinctive geographic position between continental Asia and maritime Asia.
68. Standard Meridian vs Tropic of Cancer

Do not confuse:

  • Tropic of Cancer → 23°30′ N latitude.
  • Indian Standard Meridian → 82°30′ E longitude.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

23½° N → Latitude

82½° E → Longitude

69. Latitude vs Longitude — Exam Reminder

Latitude:

  • Measures distance north or south of Equator.
  • Runs east-west on maps.

Longitude:

  • Measures distance east or west of Prime Meridian.
  • Runs north-south.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite Trap

Lines of latitude → Parallel to Equator.

Lines of longitude → Converge at poles.

70. Local Time and Longitude
  • Earth rotates 360° in approximately 24 hours.
  • Therefore, Earth rotates about 15° per hour.
  • One degree of longitude corresponds to approximately four minutes of local solar time.
📌 Formula

1° longitude → 4 minutes

15° longitude → 1 hour

71. India's Approximate Time Difference Calculation

India spans roughly 29° longitude.

29 × 4 minutes ≈ 116 minutes.

This is nearly two hours.

🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Easternmost vs Westernmost Local Solar Time → Nearly 2 Hours

72. Standard Meridian and Greenwich

Difference:

82°30′ = 82.5°

82.5 × 4 minutes = 330 minutes

330 minutes = 5 hours 30 minutes

Therefore:

IST = GMT/UTC + 5:30.

73. Tropic of Cancer and India's Climate
  • Areas south of the Tropic of Cancer are geographically tropical.
  • Areas north of it lie in subtropical latitudes.
  • India's climate, however, is also heavily controlled by the Himalayas and monsoon circulation.
  • Detailed climate will be treated separately.
74. Importance of the Himalayas to India's Location
  • The Himalayas form a major physical barrier along northern India.
  • They separate much of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau and Central Asian interior.
  • They have strongly influenced India's climate and historical accessibility.
  • Detailed Himalayan physiography belongs to Chapter 3.
75. India's Political-Geographical Structure
  • India currently consists of states and Union Territories under the Constitution.
  • For map questions, students should distinguish political boundaries from physical geographical divisions.
  • Political boundaries may change over time, whereas major physical features are much more stable.
76. Tamil Nadu — Location Link

For TNPSC, remember:

  • Tamil Nadu lies in southern peninsular India.
  • It lies south of Tropic of Cancer.
  • It has coastline along the Bay of Bengal and waters toward the Indian Ocean/Gulf of Mannar.
  • Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India.
  • Tamil Nadu faces Sri Lanka across the Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar.
  • Tamil Nadu's revised official coastline is 1,068.69 km.
77. Chennai Location Link
  • Chennai lies on India's southeastern coast.

  • Detailed coastal-plain geography will be covered later.
78. Kanyakumari Location Link
  • Kanyakumari marks the southern tip of mainland India.
  • It lies where the seas around peninsular India converge geographically.
  • It is an important map point in TNPSC examinations.

81. Current Coastline Revision — TNPSC Alert

Older notes, textbooks and question banks may still state:

India's coastline → 7,516.6 km.

The Government officially reassessed it to:

India's coastline → 11,098.81 km in 2025.

For a question explicitly asking the latest/revised official coastline, use:

11,098.81 km

For an older PYQ based on its original source year, the old answer may still appear as:

7,516.6 km

This distinction is important for upcoming examinations.

84. Why India's Location Matters Climatically

India's location influences:

  • Tropical and subtropical temperature patterns.
  • Monsoon circulation.
  • Maritime influence on peninsular India.
  • Continental influence in northern/interior regions.

Detailed mechanisms belong to Chapter 7 — Climate of India and Chapter 8 — Indian Monsoon.

85. Why India's Location Matters Economically

India's location provides:

  • Long maritime access.
  • Access to major Indian Ocean shipping routes.
  • Ports on both eastern and western coasts.
  • Connections with West Asia, Africa and Southeast Asia.
  • Strategic access toward major global sea lanes.
86. Why India's Location Matters Culturally

India's geography enabled historical movement of:

  • Traders.
  • Travellers.
  • Religious ideas.
  • Languages.
  • Art traditions.
  • Technologies.

Land routes passed through mountain corridors while maritime routes connected coastal India with distant regions.

87. Location Facts Not to Confuse with Physiography

This chapter covers:

  • Latitude.
  • Longitude.
  • Area.
  • Extent.
  • Standard Meridian.
  • Tropic of Cancer.
  • Boundaries.
  • Coastline.
  • Neighbours.
  • Island location.
  • Strategic position.

The following will be treated separately:

  • Himalayan ranges.
  • Northern Plains.
  • Plateaus.
  • Desert.
  • Coastal plains.
  • Island geology and relief.

This prevents factual duplication.

  • IST = UTC + 5:30.
  • India's east-west local solar-time difference is nearly two hours.
  • Kanyakumari is southernmost mainland point.
  • Indira Point is southernmost point of India.
  • Indira Point is on Great Nicobar.
  • Lakshadweep is in Arabian Sea.
  • Andaman and Nicobar are on the Bay of Bengal/Andaman Sea side.
  • Ten Degree Channel separates Andaman and Nicobar groups.
  • Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the main Lakshadweep group.
